In the church of Saint Pancras he made a Tyrian cloth bearing the history of the Lord’s Ascension; in Saint Mary at the Martyrs, a Tyrian cloth as above; in the title of Saint Sabina, as above; in the diaconia of Saint Boniface, as above; in the diaconia of Saint Mary called Cosmidin, as above; and in the basilica of Saints Cosmas and Damian, a cloth of Byzantine purple with a border of chrysoclavus and pearls.

### 380

Likewise, in the church of Saint Valentine he made a gold-woven vestment and another, most beautiful, made of *fundatus*. In the diaconia of Saints Nereus and Achilleus he made a vestment of *stauracium*; and in the diaconia of the holy Mother of God, called Dominica, he made a vestment of *stauracium*. This beneficent pontiff himself made, in the venerable monastery of Saint Sabas, a silver *butro* with its *canistrum*, weighing twelve pounds, and a vestment of *stauracium* with gold embroidery and pearls. Likewise, in the monastery of Saint Erasmus he made a vestment of *stauracium* with a cross and *gamadia*, together with its *paratrapeta*, and with a border of gold embroidery. He also made, in the monastery of Clivus Scaurus, a vestment of *stauracium* with a border of gold embroidery. In the title of Pammachius he made two vestments, one of *stauracium* with a border of gold embroidery, and another of *imizinum*.

The aforesaid most holy bishop newly repaired the church of the blessed apostle Andrew, situated at the thirtieth milestone of the Appian Way, at *in Silice*, together with its baptistery and porticoes. In that church he appointed a presbyter, and there he offered gifts both in silver and in vestments and books.

In the ninth indiction, with our sins pressing upon us, an earthquake suddenly occurred on the day before the Kalends of May. The church of the blessed apostle Paul was shaken by that earthquake, and all its repaired structures collapsed. When the great and illustrious pontiff saw this, he was plunged into deep distress and began to lament both the silver and the other materials that had been destroyed and broken there. But with the Lord’s favor and the blessed prince of the apostles’ protection, the aforesaid pontiff applied himself to the undertaking with all his strength. He rebuilt it on the scale on which it had formerly existed, with great and utmost vigor, and brought it into a better condition. He adorned it with marble in finer form, marbled both the presbytery and the whole church, and renewed its porticoes.

### 381

At the same time, in the nave that is above the altar, he newly restored all the roofing and other repaired structures, and there he offered three golden images: namely, those of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ and of the blessed princes of the apostles, Peter and Paul. He also placed another image, a gilded silver image of the Savior, above the doorposts at the entrance; it weighed sixty pounds. He likewise newly restored all the silverwork there that had been shattered.

He also adorned the windows of that church, of extraordinary beauty, with *cypsinum* metal.

The aforesaid pontiff made, in the basilica of the Savior called Constantiniana, two vestments above the altar: one with gold embroidery and gems, bearing the history of the Savior entering the holy city; and another, embroidered with gold and precious gems, bearing the history of the Lord’s Resurrection. Around the altar he made four red silk curtains and four white ones, with gold embroidery; three curtains before the images, with a band; and thirty-seven other white silk curtains.

At the altar of Saint Venantius he made a *fundatus* vestment with two curtains. In the oratories of Saint John the Baptist and Saint John the Evangelist he made two *stauracium* vestments with gold embroidery and two curtains.

### 382

The same prelate and pontiff made, above the altar of the blessed apostle Peter, a vestment with a vine of purest gold, with most precious gems and pearls. It bore in the center the face of the Savior, and those of the holy Mother of God Mary and the twelve apostles; he used twenty-five pounds of gold on it. He also made another gold-embroidered vestment bearing the history of the Greater Litany.

He made yet another vestment bearing three gold-embroidered panels and the history of the Lord’s Passion, with the following inscription:

> This is my body, which will be handed over for you, [Col. 1221] and so forth.

Likewise, he made a large *fundatus* curtain. He also made Paschal curtains on silver arches: five with borders of *stauracium*, ninety-three with gold embroidery; and on the arches forty-eight larger white curtains.

He also made fifteen *gabathae* of purest gold, hanging with gems in the canopy before the altar; they weighed sixty-five and a half pounds. He made a panel before the confession of purest gold, weighing twenty-nine pounds. He also placed two gilded silver images above the larger royal doors [Note: [Col. 1221] “folds” or “shutters”], weighing ninety pounds. He also made two silver *canthara* in the presbytery, weighing fifty pounds. He adorned the windows of the church with *cyprinum* metal.

### 383

In the basilica of the teacher of the world, the blessed apostle Paul, he made a gold-embroidered vestment bearing in the center the Savior, and on the right and left the blessed Peter and Paul preaching to the Gentiles, with a border of gold embroidery and precious gems.

Above the altar of Saint Andrew he made a gold-embroidered vestment with pearls. He also adorned the presbytery with carved marble. At the altar of Saint Petronilla he made a white silk vestment with gold-embroidered panels and a cross; there too he adorned the presbytery with carved marble.

He made six silver columns and two *regulares* of purest silver, weighing eighty pounds in all. Above the body of the blessed confessor and pontiff Gregory he made a white silk vestment with gold-embroidered panels and a cross.

Likewise, in the basilica of the holy Mother of God at the Manger, he made an Alexandrian curtain with a border of *stauracium*, and another white curtain with a border of *blatthin*, hanging above the altar. Before the Manger he made white curtains with a border of *blatthin*. He also made twelve curtains at the larger doors and before the sacristy, and inside the Manger he made a vestment of *alithinum* with gold embroidery.

He also made, in the basilica of the blessed martyr Lawrence outside the walls, a Tyrian curtain with a border of *stauracium*. In the basilica of the blessed martyr Pancratius he made a *ciborium* of purest silver, weighing 367 pounds.

In the title of Calixtus, in honor of the holy Mother of God and ever-virgin Mary, he made a silver *ciborium*, weighing 504½ pounds. In the title of Eudoxia he made a white vestment with a border of gold embroidery. In the title of Saint Cecilia he made a vestment of *stauracium*; in the title of Saint Eusebius, a *fundatus* vestment; and in the title of Saint Vitalis, a *stauracium* vestment with a cross of gold embroidery.

In the title of Saint Pudentiana he made a vestment as above, and in the title of Saint Anastasia he made a *fundatus* vestment. In the title of Saint Praxedes he made a *stauracium* vestment with a border of *blatthin*. In the basilica of the blessed Lawrence at *in Formoso* he made a *quadrapulum* vestment.

### 384

In the monastery of Saint Anastasius he made a vestment of the same gold embroidery, depicting the martyr’s passion, and a silver *pharus* with an octagonal *canistrum*, weighing twenty-five pounds.

In the monastery of Saint Sylvester he made two vestments: one Byzantine vestment with gold embroidery in the major basilica, and another of *fundatus* in the oratory. In the monastery of Saint Lucia at *in Renatis* he made a *fundatus* vestment with gold embroidery; in Saint Angelo at *in Fabiano* he made a *fundatus* vestment; and in the diaconia of Saint Lucia at the Seven Ways he made a *fundatus* vestment.

In the diaconia of Saints Sergius and Bacchus he made a *stauracium* vestment; in the diaconia of Saint Lucia at *in Orphea*, a *stauracium* vestment; and in the diaconia of Saint Eustachius, a *fundatus* vestment.

This venerable and beneficent pontiff, protected by God, made in the basilica of the blessed apostle Peter, his patron, a crucifix of purest silver in the middle of the basilica, weighing seventy-two pounds.

In the Lateran patriarchium he made a dining hall of extraordinary size, decorated with a mosaic apse. He also made ten other apses, on the right and left, painted with various histories and bearing apostles preaching to the Gentiles, adjoining the Constantiniana basilica. In that place he installed couches and, in the center, a porphyry basin pouring forth water. He also paved its floor with various marbles.

In the title of Saint Quiriacus he made a *stauracium* vestment with a border of *blatthin*, gold embroidery around it, and a pearl cross in the center. In the cemetery of Saint Sixtus on the Appian Way he made a *stauracium* vestment with a cross of gold embroidery in the center.

In the title of Calixtus, above the altar behind the apse, he made a *stauracium* vestment with a cross of gold embroidery in the center; there likewise he made six *stauracium* curtains. In the title of the Four Crowned Saints he made a *stauracium* vestment bearing a gold-embroidered cross in the center. In the title of Saint Marcellus he made a *stauracium* vestment.

### 385

Likewise, in the church of the holy martyr Sabina he made a *fundatus* vestment with a border of *blatthin*, bearing a gold-embroidered cross in the center. In the basilica of Saint Lawrence at *in Formoso* he made a *fundatus* vestment.

The church of the blessed apostle Paul called Conventus, situated in the territory of Orbetello, within the boundaries of Suana, Cusa, Tuscia, and Castrum, had already rotted away through excessive age, and cattle were taking refuge in it; moreover, its relics had been removed. The same most holy pontiff ordered it to be cleansed, newly restored all its roofing and other repaired structures in the porticoes, placed a *stauracium* vestment on its altar, and ordered the relics to be reinterred.

Likewise, in the basilica of the blessed apostle Peter situated at Albano, which was already on the point of collapse from excessive age, he newly restored all its roofs and repaired structures.

The same beneficent pontiff made, in the basilica of the blessed martyr Hippolytus in the city of Porto, two *stauracium* vestments, one over his body and the other on the principal altar. In the title of the holy martyr Sabina he made four *stauracium* curtains with a border of *blatthin*. In the oratory of the holy Mother of God situated in the hospice at Firmum he made a most beautiful *stauracium* vestment.

### 386

This pontiff, protected by God and illustrious, established that litanies should be celebrated for the three days before the Lord’s Ascension: namely, on Monday, when the pontiff went out with all the clergy and the entire people, with hymns and spiritual songs, proceeding from the church of the Mother of God at the Manger to the church of the Savior called Constantiniana; on Tuesday, when they went out from the church of the holy martyr Sabina and proceeded to the blessed apostle Paul; and on Wednesday, when they went out from the church of Jerusalem and proceeded to the blessed church of the martyr Lawrence outside the walls.

He also made, in the title of the Crowned Saints, a *stauracium* vestment bearing a gold-embroidered cross in the center.

### 387

The same most holy prelate made, in the basilica of the blessed martyr Agapitus in the city of Praeneste, a *stauracium* vestment with a border of *fundatus* and a gold-embroidered cross in the center.

The same most holy prelate made, in the church of the blessed Clement situated at Velitrae, a *stauracium* vestment. Likewise, in the title of the blessed Chrysogonus he made a *stauracium* vestment with a border of *blatthin*; in the title of the blessed Lawrence at *in Lucina*, a *stauracium* vestment with a border of *blatthin*; in the title of the blessed Mark, a *stauracium* vestment with a border; and in the title of the blessed Lawrence at *in Damaso*, a similar vestment.

Likewise, in the title of the blessed Sixtus he made a *stauracium* vestment with a border of *blatthin*. He also did so in the diaconia of the blessed Hadrian, in the church of the blessed Martina, and in the ancient diaconia: he made *stauracium* vestments with borders.

In the diaconia of the blessed Archangel he made three vestments, one of *stauracium* with a border of *blatthin*, and the other two of Tyrian cloth with borders of *fundatus*, bearing a history of elephants.

In the diaconia of Saint Theodore he made a *stauracium* vestment with a border. In the diaconia of the blessed George he made a *fundatus* vestment bearing a history of elephants, or various histories, with a border of *fundatus*. In the surrounding diaconia he made a *stauracium* vestment with a border of *blatthin*. Likewise, in the diaconia on the Via Lata he made two Tyrian vestments with borders of *blatthin*.

### 388

In the diaconia of Saint Agatha he made a *stauracium* vestment with a border of *blatthin*. In the basilica of the blessed Archangel situated at the Seventh Milestone he made a *stauracium* vestment with a border of *blatthin*. In the monastery of Saint Agapitus situated at *ad Vincula* he made a *stauracium* vestment.

The same most merciful prelate made, in the church of the blessed martyr Agnes, where her body rests, a *fundatus* vestment with a border of *blatthin*. In the church of the blessed Apollinaris he made a *stauracium* vestment with a border of *blatthin*.

The same most merciful prelate made, in the title of Saints Martin and Sylvester, two *stauracium* vestments, one with a border of *fundatus* and the other with a border of *blatthin*. In the diaconia of Saint Vitus he made a *stauracium* vestment with a border of *fundatus*.

In the church of the blessed Eugenia, where her holy body rests, he made a *stauracium* vestment with a border of *blatthin*. In the church of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill he made two *stauracium* vestments, one for the principal altar and the other over the bodies of the holy martyrs Primus and Felicianus.

Likewise, in the basilica of the blessed Euphemia he made a *stauracium* vestment; and in the basilica of the blessed Archangel situated in the Vicus Patricius he made a *stauracium* vestment.

### 389

Above the tomb of the blessed martyr Sebastian on the Appian Way at the Catacombs he made two large vestments, one of *stauracium* and the other of *fundatus*. There, above the tombs of the apostles Peter and Paul, he made two vestments, of *stauracium*, *fundatus*, or *blatthin*.

The same most holy prelate made, in the basilica of the blessed martyr Lawrence situated within the city of Tibur, a *stauracium* vestment. In the oratory of Saint Stephen at Saint Peter, which is called Major, he made a *stauracium* vestment.

In the basilica of the blessed Hyacinthus situated in the Sabine territory, where his body also rests, he made a most beautiful *stauracium* vestment.

Likewise, this pontiff, protected by God and illustrious, made above the altar of the blessed apostle Peter, his patron, a gold-embroidered vestment of extraordinary size, bearing the history of the Lord’s Nativity and decorated with most precious gems and pearls.

In the aforesaid church he made *stauracium* and *fundatus* curtains, hanging between the larger columns on the right and left, sixty-five in number. He also made three larger white silk curtains hanging before the royal doors at the entrance.

There, too, his Blessedness made a crucifix of purest silver, standing beside the principal altar, of extraordinary size and ornamentation; it weighed fifty-two pounds. Above it he made six *gabathae* with a cross, of purest silver, hanging before the great arch on the right and left; together they weighed twelve and a half pounds.

### 390

There likewise the illustrious pontiff made *stauracium* curtains hanging on silver arches around the altar and in the presbytery, ninety-six in number. Two of them bore crosses of gold embroidery in the center with roundels, and another eight had borders of gold embroidery.

He also made the arches with their columns in the aforesaid church of purest silver; in the middle of the presbytery they weighed 251½ pounds in all.

The same beneficent pontiff made, in the place mentioned above, an interlaced, repoussé cross of the purest gold, hanging in the canopy before the altar, with twelve candles; it weighed thirteen pounds.

The aforesaid venerable pontiff also made, in the basilica of the teacher of the world, the blessed apostle Paul, large *fundatus* chalices of purest silver from that apostle’s gifts. Eleven hung in the great arch, and another forty hung between the larger columns on the right and left; together they weighed 267 pounds.

This same beneficent prelate, filled with divine inspiration, made in the basilica of the blessed apostle Paul a *ciborium* with its columns above the altar, of extraordinary size and beauty, decorated with purest silver; it weighed 2,015 pounds. He also made a repoussé, incised cross of purest gold, hanging in the canopy before the altar; it weighed thirteen pounds. He made as well a red curtain hanging before the altar, bearing in the center a gold-embroidered cross and a border of gold embroidery.

### 391

Likewise, in the basilica of the holy Mother of God at the Manger he made five *gabathae* of purest gold, weighing eight and a half pounds, and a cross of purest gold, weighing ten pounds. He also made a large crown of purest silver, weighing thirty-six pounds.

There he made forty-two white silk curtains hanging between the larger columns on the right and left, eleven of them rose-colored. Around the altar mentioned above he also made four other rose-colored white silk curtains hanging from the arch of the *ciborium*, one of them with gold embroidery and pearls, as well as another larger white curtain hanging before the larger royal doors at the entrance.

He newly repaired all the roofing and other structures of the church of the blessed Aerea situated at Ostia. The church of the blessed Marcellus, situated at the fourteenth milestone, had been burned by fire; the same beneficent prelate restored it completely.

In the basilica of the Savior called Constantiniana the illustrious pontiff made four white silk curtains around the altar, one of them bearing in the center a panel with a gold-embroidered cross.

In the same basilica of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ he renewed the principal altar, of extraordinary size, decorated with purest silver; it weighed sixty-nine pounds.

In the basilica of the holy Mother of God at the Manger he made a gold-embroidered vestment adorned with pearls, bearing the history of the Lord’s Nativity. He also made two silver arches in the presbytery with four columns, and five other arches; together they weighed 133 pounds.

The same principal prelate made, in the basilica of the holy Mother of God at the Manger, a red *alithynus* vestment bearing in the center a gold-embroidered panel with the history of our Lord Jesus Christ and Saint Simeon, when He was presented in the Temple; around it was a band of gold embroidery.

He also made another gold-embroidered vestment of extraordinary size and beauty, bearing the history of the holy Mother of God’s Dormition, decorated with precious gems and adorned with pearls, with a border of gold embroidery and a band of gold embroidery around it.

In the diaconia of that holy Mother of God, our Lady, called Dominica, he made a red *alithynus* vestment bearing in the center a gold-embroidered panel with the history of that same Mother of God, adorned with pearls and with a border of gold embroidery.

In the diaconia of that holy Mother of God, called Antiqua, he made above the principal altar a *ciborium* of purest silver, weighing 212 pounds.

### 392

The aforesaid venerable and illustrious pontiff made, in the basilica of the blessed apostle Peter, his patron, a repoussé *gabatha* of purest gold, adorned with precious gems. It hangs before the image of that apostle at the entrance to the vestibule and weighs seven and a half pounds.

From bottom to top he covered the face of the sacred altar of that prince of the apostles with gold, together with the lower and upper lights; and inside the confession, the standing Savior, with the blessed apostles Peter and Paul on His right and left, both wearing crowns of precious gems. He also covered the pavement of that confession with highly refined gold. Altogether it weighed 453 pounds and six ounces.

Above that sacred altar he made a gold-embroidered vestment bearing the history of the Lord’s Ascension and Pentecost, with a border of gold embroidery.

### 393

Likewise, in the place mentioned above, he made an image of that prince of the apostles in the men’s gate, of purest gold and decorated with precious gems, of extraordinary size and beauty; it weighed nineteen pounds and three ounces.

Above all, the same most blessed pontiff made cast grilles at the entrance to the presbytery, on the right and left, and also at the entrance to the vestibule, of very pure silver; together they weighed 1,573 pounds.

He also made eight pairs of movable columns—[Note: [Col. 1225] “turned” or “revolving”—both at the entrance to the central body, on the right and left, on the men’s and women’s sides; together they weighed 190 pounds. He also made eight silver arches, weighing 143 pounds in all.

The same most blessed pontiff made, in the basilica of the blessed Andrew mentioned above, a *regnum* of purest gold adorned with precious gems; it weighed two pounds and five ounces.

Likewise, above the altar of Saint Petronilla mentioned above, he made a golden *regnum* with precious gems; it weighed two pounds and [Col. 1227] three ounces.

In the same way, above the altar of the holy Mother of God mentioned above, called Mediana, he made a *fundatus* vestment with a border of gold embroidery, bearing the history of the Lord’s Annunciation.

The same most blessed pontiff made, in the basilica of the teacher of the world, the blessed apostle Paul, forty-seven *canistri* of pure silver; together they weighed 247 pounds.

In the monastery of the holy martyr Agatha above the Subura he made a red *alithynus* vestment bearing in the center a gold-embroidered panel with a border of gold embroidery.

In the monastery of Saint Pancratius, situated behind the basilica of the Savior called Constantiniana, he made a *fundatus* vestment.

Here he made for the blessed apostle Peter, his patron, a golden Gospel book adorned around the edges with green, hyacinth-colored, and white gems of extraordinary size; it weighed seventeen pounds and four ounces.

Here he made a distinguished golden chalice adorned with various precious stones; it weighed twenty-eight pounds. Likewise, he made a golden paten weighing twenty-eight pounds and nine ounces.

### 394

Likewise, in the basilica of that apostle he made four gilded cherubim of purest silver, standing on the capitals of silver columns beneath the *ciborium*; they weighed ninety-three pounds.

The same principal prelate also made, in the place mentioned above, a golden image of the Savior standing on the beam above the entrance to the vestibule; it weighed seventy-nine pounds.

In the basilica of the teacher of the world, the blessed apostle Paul, he made two angels of gilded purest silver, standing beside the image of the Savior at the entrance to the vestibule; they weighed 100½ pounds.

He also made a porphyry *polycandilum*, hanging in the canopy before the confession on golden chains; the chains weighed one pound.

At the entrance to the basilica mentioned above he made five larger images of silver for the royal doors; together they weighed 229 pounds.

There likewise he made two pairs of gilded *aquamanus antipemta*; together they weighed fourteen pounds.

The same prophetic prelate made, in the place mentioned above, large movable repoussé *cerostata* of purest silver; together they weighed eighty-six pounds and eight ounces. He also made two large cast *bimyx* lamps, weighing fifty-seven pounds, and his Blessedness established that they should burn every night before the altar of that apostle.

Here, inspired by divine grace, he covered the great beam beneath the principal arch with very pure silver; it weighed 1,352 pounds.

### 395

The illustrious pontiff made, in the place mentioned above, a gold-embroidered vestment of extraordinary size and beauty for the principal altar. It bore the history of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, His holy Mother, and the twelve apostles, with a border of gold embroidery, adorned everywhere with pearls, and decorated on both sides with *blatthin* and gold embroidery. The distinguished prelate established that it should be placed there on the feasts of the apostles.

There, above the great cross, he made a *panoclysta* of highly refined gold, adorned with precious gems; it weighed forty-two pounds and two ounces. He also made four pairs of *cerostata*, covered with gilded silver; together they weighed seventy-seven pounds.

The venerable and illustrious pontiff made, above the altar of Saint Petronilla, a *ciborium* of purest silver with porphyry columns, of extraordinary size; it weighed 348 pounds. He also made a standing silver image beneath the arch of that *ciborium*, weighing ten and a half pounds.

This pontiff, protected by God and illustrious, made in the basilica of the teacher of the world, the blessed apostle Paul, above the principal altar, a gold-embroidered vestment bearing the history of the Lord’s Resurrection, adorned with pearls and with a border of gold embroidery.

Likewise, he made two images of the apostles, adorned with pearls, of gilded silver; together they weighed eighty-six pounds.

### 396

This most merciful pontiff made, in the basilica of the holy Mother of God at the Manger, above the altar, a gold-embroidered vestment bearing the history of the Lord’s Resurrection, decorated with extraordinary size and beauty, with a border of gold embroidery and adorned everywhere with pearls.

In the title of the holy Mother of God called Calixtus he made a *regnum* of purest gold, hanging above the principal altar and adorned with precious gems; it weighed one pound.

In the diaconia of that holy Mother of God, called Dominica, he made a *regnum* of pure gold, hanging above the principal altar and adorned with precious gems; it weighed two pounds.

This most blessed prelate, filled with divine inspiration, made in the basilica of the Mother of God at the Manger, at the entrance to the Manger, royal doors of purest silver; together they weighed 127 pounds. Above these royal doors he placed a small *fundatus* curtain with a gold-embroidered band around it.

He also made three other Tyrian curtains above the larger royal doors at the entrance to the basilica, with borders of *fundatus*.

### 397

The same distinguished prelate made, in the basilica of the blessed apostle Peter, large chalices of very pure silver, resting on silver beams, eighteen in number; together they weighed 182 pounds.

There likewise he made large cast *cerostata* of purest silver, standing before the confession; they weighed 198 pounds.

He covered the silver beam above the golden image at the entrance to the vestibule; it weighed 126½ pounds.

He also made two cast lamps of purest silver; together they weighed twenty-seven pounds. He established that on Sundays and on holy solemnities they should stand on either side beside the *ectoria* [reading uncertain] and shine with the splendor of their light for the reading of the sacred lessons.

Here he made for the blessed apostle Andrew a *ciborium* of purest silver above the principal altar; it weighed 305 pounds.

This principal pontiff, inspired by God, observed that the baptistery mentioned above was already close to ruin through excessive age and that the space was too confined for the people coming to baptism. He therefore rebuilt the baptistery from its foundations on a broad circular plan and brought it into better condition. He established the sacred font in the center in a more spacious area, adorned it around with porphyry columns, and placed a column in the middle of the font. Above the column he set a lamb of purest silver pouring out water; it weighed eighteen pounds and ten ounces.

He also constructed the principal altar beneath the apse. He covered its face and confession, or folds, for the adornment of the sacred altar with very pure silver; together they weighed forty-eight pounds. He also placed a *stauracium* vestment over it and made a *regular* there, overlaid with purest silver.

Above that *regular* he placed a silver arch and *gamadia*; together they weighed eighty pounds. He also placed three images, as mentioned above, weighing thirty-seven pounds and ten ounces.

He adorned the baptistery itself around with various paintings.

### 398

The oratory of the Holy Cross mentioned above, which was on the point of collapse through excessive age, this principal shepherd rebuilt from its foundations together with its apse, using a new structure, and brought it to completion. He adorned the apse itself with mosaic, various paintings, and marbles of marvelous splendor.

There he also offered a *ciborium* with its columns above the altar and covered the face of the altar with purest silver; it weighed 121 pounds and two ounces. He made a *spanoclystum* *regnum* of purest gold, with a cross in the center, hanging above that altar; it weighed one pound and eleven ounces.

He also made four additional silver columns, and above those columns a *regular* overlaid with purest silver; it weighed sixty-four pounds and three ounces. He made three silver arches, weighing forty-three pounds and eight ounces; three gilded silver images, weighing thirty pounds; and twelve interlaced silver *canistri*, weighing seventy-eight pounds in all.

He made twenty-one interlaced *gabathae* of silver and one cross, weighing fifty pounds altogether. He made one *fundatus* vestment for the altar; another of *blatthin* with gold embroidery; and another white rose-colored vestment with gold embroidery.

He made a small gold-embroidered curtain with a crucifix and decorated with pearls; seven *stauracium* curtains; four *fundatus* curtains; and six small Tyrian curtains hanging on the *regular* before the images.

He made twelve white silk curtains, adorned around with *fundatus*; one larger white rose-colored curtain, decorated above with *quadrapulum*; and another red curtain with *bubalus*, hanging before the larger royal doors.

He made four small *stauracium* curtains hanging on the *regular* before the images, and eleven other assorted silk curtains.

At the fonts, in the place mentioned above, he made three Tyrian curtains hanging on the *regular* before the images, and twenty-one other silk curtains.

### 399

Here he made for the blessed apostle Peter, his patron, a distinguished golden *spanoclystum* chalice adorned with various precious stones; it weighed thirty pounds.

Likewise, he made a golden *spanoclysta* paten, similarly adorned with various precious stones; it weighed twenty-five pounds.

Above the *ciborium* of the principal altar of the blessed apostle Peter he made four large *canthara* of purest silver, bearing gilded silver candles in the center; together they weighed 140 pounds.

The aforesaid illustrious pontiff made, in the place mentioned above, an apostolic thurible of purest gold; it weighed two pounds and five ounces.

He made a gold-embroidered vestment for the principal altar, decorated with various paintings, which he established should be placed there four times each year during the twelve readings.

In the place mentioned above he made four large crowns of purest silver; together they weighed 154½ pounds.

There he also made a *lectorium* of purest silver, of extraordinary size; it weighed 143 pounds. He also made *cerostata* of very pure silver, standing beside that *lectorium*; together they weighed forty-nine pounds.

Above those *cerostata* he made two cast *bimyx* lamps of pure silver; they weighed twenty-seven pounds. He established that on Sundays and on holy solemnities they should stand on either side beside the *lectorium* and shine with the splendor of their light for the reading of the sacred lessons.

In the presbytery he made fourteen *pharocanthara* of very pure silver; together they weighed 433 pounds. He also made eight columns and four arches of silver; there they weighed 173 pounds.

### 400

In the place mentioned above he made sixty-four cast silver chalices hanging between the larger columns on the right and left of the basilica; together they weighed 461 pounds.

The same prophetic prelate, in the place mentioned above, covered the principal altar of the blessed apostle Andrew with gilded purest silver, adorned with marvelous beauty; it weighed 135 pounds throughout. He made twelve *canthara* of purest silver, weighing fifty-two pounds in all, and twelve silver *canistri*, weighing seventy-eight pounds.

He covered the altar of the blessed Petronilla with gilded purest silver, adorned everywhere with various paintings; it weighed 162 pounds and eight ounces.

He also covered the altar of the blessed confessor and pontiff Gregory entirely with gilded silver; it weighed 127 pounds.

In the place mentioned above, in the midst of the basilica of the blessed apostle Peter, he made a large Alexandrian silk curtain bearing a *fundatus* panel in the center and adorned around with *fundatus*.

The same principal prelate also made two apostolic thuribles of purest gold. One he placed inside above the apostle’s body; it weighed two pounds. The other weighed two pounds and eight ounces and preceded the processions.

### 401

This beneficent prelate made two apostolic thuribles of the purest gold in the basilica of the holy Apostle Paul. This beneficent prelate also clad the front of the altar of the holy Mother of God at the Praesepe in the purest gilded silver, weighing 86 pounds. There he made two crowns of the purest silver, weighing 54 pounds. He made large Alexandrian curtains of silk, decorated around with *fundatum*.

This distinguished prelate, through the generosity of almighty God and of blessed Peter, the key-bearer of the kingdom of heaven, offered throughout the sacred churches of the saints in this blessed city of Rome crowns and also canisters of the purest silver, for the remission of his sins; namely:

In the church of our Lord and Savior, which is called Constantinian, he made crowns of the purest silver, weighing 23 pounds. In the basilica of the holy Mother of God at the Praesepe, likewise, he made a crown of pure silver, weighing 13 pounds. In the basilica of the holy Mother of God at the title of Calixtus, he made a silver crown, weighing 13 pounds and 3 ounces. In the diaconia of that same Mother of God, which is called the Ancient, he likewise made a silver crown, weighing 13 pounds. In the church of the holy Mother of God at the Martyrs, he made a silver crown, weighing 12 pounds and 3 ounces. In the diaconia of that same Mother of God, which is called Cosmedin, he likewise made a crown of silver, weighing 12 pounds. Also in the diaconia of the holy Mother of God, which is called Dominica, he likewise made a crown of silver, weighing 9 pounds. In the diaconia of the holy Mother of God situated on the Via Lata, he made a silver crown, weighing 9 pounds. In the diaconia of Saint Mary in Cyro, he made a silver crown, weighing 8 pounds. Moreover, in the diaconia of the blessed Mother of God situated outside the gate of the holy Apostle Peter, he made a silver crown, weighing 5 pounds and 3 ounces. In the diaconia of that same Mother of God situated at the Hadrian, he likewise made a silver crown, weighing 5 pounds.

### 402

Also in the oratory of the holy Mother of God situated in the Xenodochium of Firmus, he made a silver canister, weighing 2 pounds and 7 ounces. In the church of the holy Apostle Peter he made a canister of the purest silver, weighing 22 pounds; and in the church of the holy Apostle Paul he likewise made a canister of the purest silver, weighing 22 pounds, 4 ounces, and 8 [ounces]. Moreover, in the church of the holy Apostle Andrew, which is called Eudoxia’s, he likewise made a silver crown, weighing 9 pounds. Furthermore, in the church of the holy John the Baptist, situated beside the Lateran patriarchate, he made a silver crown, weighing 5 pounds. Moreover, in the church of the holy Evangelist John, situated at the place mentioned above, he made a silver crown, weighing 5 pounds. Likewise, in the church of Saint Stephen, situated on the Caelian Hill, he similarly made a silver crown, weighing 7 pounds and 11 ounces. In the basilica of the Apostles, situated on the Via Lata, he made a silver crown, weighing 13 pounds. In the mausoleum of the blessed Petronilla, situated at the church of the holy Apostle Peter, he made a silver crown, weighing 20 pounds. In the church of Jerusalem, situated at the Sessorian, he made a silver crown, weighing 5 pounds. In the church of the holy Lawrence, situated outside the walls, he likewise made a silver crown, weighing 13 pounds. In the church of the holy martyr Apollinaris he made a crown, weighing 5 pounds and 4 ounces. Furthermore, in the basilica of the holy martyr Pancratius, situated outside the walls, he likewise made a silver crown, weighing 8 pounds. He also made, in the church of the holy martyr Valentine, situated outside the walls, where his body rests, a silver crown weighing 6 pounds. In the title of the holy martyr and pontiff Clement he made a silver crown, weighing 15 pounds.

### 403

In the title of the blessed Aquila and Prisca he made a silver crown, weighing 6 pounds. In the title of Saint Balbina he likewise made one. Moreover, in the church of the holy martyr and pontiff Sixtus he likewise made a crown. In the title of the holy martyr Lawrence, which is called that of Lucina, he likewise made one, weighing 4 pounds and 10 ounces. In the title of the holy martyr Lawrence, which is called that of Damasus, he made a silver crown, weighing 5 pounds. In the church of that same martyr, situated at Formosus, he made a silver canister, weighing 2 pounds and 7 ounces. In the title of Pammachius he also made a silver crown, weighing 10 pounds. In the title of Aemiliana he likewise made a silver crown, weighing 4 pounds. Also in the title of Saint Eusebius he made a silver crown, weighing 6 pounds. In the title of Praxedis he made a crown, weighing 5 pounds. In the title of Pudens he made a silver crown, weighing 9 pounds. Moreover, in the title of the blessed martyr Vitalis he made a silver crown, weighing 9 pounds and 3 ounces. In the title of the holy martyr Susanna he likewise made a crown, weighing 17 pounds. [Col. 1233]

In the title of Saint Cyriacus he made a silver crown, weighing 5 pounds. In the title of the blessed martyr Marcellus he made a silver crown, weighing 10 pounds. Also in the title of the blessed martyr Mark he likewise made one. In the title of the blessed Anastasia he made a crown, weighing 7 pounds and 9 ounces. Also in the title of Cecilia he likewise made a silver crown, weighing 10 pounds and 1 ounce altogether. In the title of the blessed martyr Chrysogonus he made a silver crown, weighing 5 pounds.

### 404

Furthermore, in the diaconia of Saints Nereus and Achilleus he made a silver crown, weighing 6 pounds and 5 ounces. In the diaconia of Saint Lucia, situated at the Seven Ways, he made a silver crown, weighing 6 pounds and 7 ounces. In the diaconia of Saint Boniface he likewise made a crown, weighing 7 pounds. In the diaconia of Saint George he made a silver crown, weighing 5 pounds. In the diaconia of Saint Theodore he likewise made a crown, weighing 6 pounds and 8 ounces. In the diaconia of Saints Sergius and Bacchus he made a silver crown, weighing 6 pounds. In the diaconia of Saints Cosmas and Damian he made a crown, weighing 5 pounds and 8 ounces. In the diaconia of the holy martyr Hadrian he made a silver crown, weighing 6 pounds. In the diaconia of the holy Archangel he also made a silver crown, weighing 6 pounds. In the diaconia of Saint Eustachius he likewise made one, weighing 6 pounds and 5 ounces. In the diaconia of Saint Lucia, situated beside the Orpheus, he likewise made a silver crown, weighing 6 pounds and 2 ounces. At the same time, in the diaconia of the blessed martyr Vitus, situated at the Macellum, he made a silver crown, weighing 6 pounds. Moreover, in the diaconia of Saint Agatha he likewise made a silver crown, weighing 5 pounds. He also made, in the diaconia of Saint Sylvester, situated beside the holy Apostle Peter, a silver crown weighing 4 pounds. Furthermore, in the diaconia of Saint Martin, situated beside the holy Apostle Peter, he likewise made a silver crown, weighing 5 pounds and 3 ounces. In the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin, situated beside the Orpheus, he made a silver crown, weighing 6 pounds and 2 ounces.

### 405

This pontiff, protected by God and distinguished, made a silver crown in the monastery of Saint Sabas, weighing 8 pounds and 10 ounces. Furthermore, in the monastery of the blessed martyr Anastasius he likewise made a silver crown, weighing 8 pounds, 4 ounces, and a half. In the monastery of Saint Andrew, situated on the Caurus Hills, he likewise made a crown of pure silver, weighing 5 pounds. In the monastery of the blessed martyr Agatha, situated above the Subura, he likewise made one. Also in the monastery of Saint Erasmus, situated on the Caelian Hill, he made a crown, weighing 4 pounds and 2 ounces. In the same way, in the monastery of Saint Sylvester, he made a silver crown weighing 6 pounds and 3 ounces. In the monastery of the holy martyr Lawrence, which is called Pallacini, he made a silver canister, weighing 2 pounds and 7 ounces. Indeed, in the monastery of Saint Pancratius, situated beside the basilica of the Savior, he made a silver crown weighing 5 and a half pounds. He also made, in the monastery of Saints Andrew and Bartholomew, which is called Honorius’s, a silver canister weighing 3 pounds. In the monastery of Saint Stephen, situated beside the Lateran, he made a silver canister weighing 2 pounds. At the same time, in the monastery of that first martyr Stephen, situated at the church of the holy Apostle Peter, he made a silver canister weighing 3 and a half pounds. This beneficent prelate made, in the monastery of Saints John and Paul, situated beside the holy Apostle Peter, a silver canister weighing 3 pounds. Likewise, in the monastery of Saint Martin, situated at the place mentioned above, he made a canister weighing 4 pounds and 2 ounces. In the monastery of Saint Stephen mentioned above, which is called Catagalla Patritia, he likewise made a silver canister weighing 2 and a half pounds. At the same time, in the monastery of Saint Caesarius, situated at the church of the holy Apostle Paul, he likewise made a silver canister weighing 3 pounds. In the monastery of Saint Stephen mentioned above he made a canister weighing 2 pounds. Moreover, in the monastery of Saints Cosmas and Damian, situated beside the Praesepe, he made a silver canister weighing 2 pounds and 2 ounces. In the same way, in the monastery of Saint Andrew, which is called Massa Juliana, he made a silver canister weighing 2 pounds. Also, in the monastery of Saint Hadrian, situated beside the Praesepe, he likewise made a canister weighing 2 pounds. In the monastery of Saint Cassian, situated beside the holy martyr Lawrence outside the walls, he made a silver canister weighing 2 pounds.

### 406

He also made, in the monastery of Saint Stephen, situated at the place mentioned above, a silver canister weighing 2 and a half pounds. Furthermore, in the monastery of Saint Victor, situated at Saint Pancratius, he made a silver canister weighing 2 pounds and 7 ounces. In the monastery of Saint Chrysogonus he likewise made a canister weighing 3 pounds. This beneficent prelate made, in the monastery of Saint Mary, which is called Ambrose’s, a silver canister weighing 2 pounds. Likewise, in the monastery of Saint Mary, which is called Julia’s, at the place mentioned above, he made one. In the monastery of Saint Andrew, situated beside the basilica of the Apostles, he likewise made one. At the same time, in the oratory of Saint Stephen, situated at Dulcitius, he made a silver canister weighing 2 pounds and 5 ounces. Indeed, in the oratory of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, situated at Callinicus, he likewise made a canister. Moreover, in the monastery of Saint Agapitus, situated beside the title of Eudoxia, he likewise made a silver canister, weighing [a half pound?; the text is defective].

[Col. 1235] In the same way, in the oratory of Saint Agnes, situated in the monastery called the Two Furnaces, he made a silver canister weighing 2 pounds and 8 ounces. Also, in the oratory of Saint Vitus, situated in the monastery called “of the Sardians,” he made a silver canister weighing 3 pounds. In the monastery of Saint Bibiana he likewise made a silver canister weighing 2 pounds and 9 ounces. He also made, in the oratory of Saint Lucia, situated in the monastery of Renatus, a silver canister weighing 2 pounds.

### 407

Furthermore, in the oratory of Saint Mary, situated in the monastery of Michael, he likewise made a silver canister weighing 2 pounds and 2 ounces. In the monastery of Saint Sergius he likewise made a silver canister weighing 3 pounds. This beneficent prelate also made, in the oratory of Saint Agatha, situated in the monastery at Africus, a silver canister weighing 3 pounds. Likewise, in the monastery of Saints Euphemia and the Archangel, situated beside the title of Pudens, he made a silver canister weighing 5 pounds. In the monastery of Saint Isidore he likewise made a canister. At the same time, in the oratory of Saint Agatha, situated in the monastery of Tempulus, he likewise made a canister. In the oratory of Saint Caesarius, situated in the monastery of Corsas, he likewise made a canister weighing 2 pounds and 3 ounces. Indeed, in the monastery of Saint Semitrius he likewise made a silver canister. Moreover, in the oratory of Saint Mary, situated in the monastery of the Aqua Salvias, he likewise made one. In the same way, in the monastery of Saint Donatus, situated beside the title of Saint Prisca, he made a silver canister weighing 2 pounds and 5 ounces. In the monastery of Saint John, situated on the Aventine, he likewise made a silver canister weighing 2 pounds. Also, in the oratory of Saint Mary, situated in the monastery of Lutara, he made silver canisters weighing 2 and a half pounds. He also made, in the monastery of Jerusalem, situated at the church of the holy Apostle Peter, a silver canister weighing 2 pounds.

### 408

Furthermore, in the monastery of Saint Agnes, situated outside the Nomentan Gate, he made silver canisters weighing 5 pounds. In the monastery of Saint Eugenia, situated outside the Latin Gate, he likewise made a silver canister weighing 5 pounds. Also, in the oratory of Saint Gregory, situated in the Campus Martius, he made silver canisters weighing 3 pounds.

This beneficent prelate made, in the title of the blessed Sabina, a crown of the purest silver weighing 8 pounds. Likewise, in the diaconia of Saints Sylvester and Martin, situated beside the Orpheus, he made a silver crown weighing 6 pounds and 2 ounces. Also, in the oratory of Saint Lucia, situated in the Xenodochium, he likewise made a silver canister weighing 2 pounds and 4 ounces. He also made, in the oratory of Saint Abbacyrus, situated in the Xenodochium, a canister weighing 2 pounds. And in the oratory of Saints Cosmas and Damian, situated in the Xenodochium called Tucium, he likewise made a silver canister weighing 2 pounds and 1 ounce. Furthermore, in the oratory of Saint Peregrinus, situated in the Lord’s hospital at the Naumachia, he made silver canisters weighing 5 pounds and 1 ounce.

The aforesaid pontiff made, in the basilica of our Lord Jesus Christ, which is called Constantinian, over the high altar, two *chrysoclaved* vestments: one bearing the scene of the Lord’s Resurrection, and the other bearing the scene of the life-giving and venerable Cross of the Lord. He made eight canthari (large vessels) of the purest silver, weighing 27 pounds and 6 ounces altogether. At the place mentioned above he clad the *rugae* before the entrance to the altar in the purest silver, weighing 48 pounds and 8 ounces. He made crowns of the purest silver, weighing 12 pounds. At the place mentioned above, at the fountains, he made ten white silk curtains, decorated around with *fundatum* and *quadrapulum*. He completely restored anew the roof and fabric of that church, together with the four-sided portico and the fountains. He also enclosed and decorated the windows of the apse with glass of various colors. He repaired the other windows of the basilica with Cyprian metal; and in the body of the basilica he made two curtains, one larger, white and *fundata*, and the other smaller, white and rose-colored.

### 409

The same prelate made in the basilica of the holy Mother of God, which is called at the Praesepe, a rose-colored curtain with a *periclysin* of *fundatum*. He made two canthari (large vessels) of the purest silver there, weighing 23 pounds. Two columns, weighing 21 pounds and 5 ounces. A cross with a *gabatha* of pure silver, weighing 5 pounds altogether.

In the diaconia of that same Mother of God, which is called the Ancient, he made four *tetravela alithyna*, decorated around with *quadrapulum*. In the oratory of Saint Andrew, at the place mentioned above, he made two silk curtains, decorated as above. In the title of that same Mother of God, which is called Calixtus’s, he made a white, rose-colored silk vestment, having in the middle a panel of *chrysoclavus* with the scene of the Presentation of our Lord Jesus Christ and Saint Simeon, with a *periclysin* of Tyrian [purple]. Four red *tetravela alithyna*, bearing crosses with *gammadia* and around them a *periclysin* of Tyrian [purple]. One large Tyrian curtain hanging before the image, with a *periclysin* of *blatthinum*. Three small red *alithyna* curtains, with a *stauracium* in the middle, hanging before the silver images, with a *periclysin* of *blatthinum*. He also made one large silk curtain in the body of the basilica and gilded silver images. Of these, one was adorned with gems; one silver arch, with its *gammadia*. Above the *cerostata*, one *pharus*; two thuribles,

[Col. 1237] weighing 95 pounds and 7 ounces altogether.

The same prophetic bishop made for the holy Apostle Peter a golden chalice, adorned with various precious stones, which leads in the processions, weighing 13 pounds. He made in the basilica of that apostle a *chrysoclaved* curtain hanging above at the entrance of the vestibule. Likewise, another larger curtain of *chrysoclavus*, hanging from the silver beam before the image of the Savior above at the entrance of the vestibule; one large crown of the purest silver, weighing 53 pounds and 8 ounces; one silver *pharus* hanging beneath that crown, weighing 23 pounds. Likewise, four silver crowns, weighing 57 pounds altogether. Eight canisters, weighing 40 pounds altogether.

### 410

Here, out of love for and in defense of the orthodox faith, he made, at the place mentioned above, two silver shields, each inscribed with the Creed: one in Greek letters and the other in Latin letters. They were placed on the right and left above the entrance to the body of the church and weighed 94 pounds and 6 ounces there.

At the place mentioned above, in the body of the basilica, he made one large *fundata* silk curtain, decorated around with *fundatum*. One large white, rose-colored silk curtain, hanging from the large beam above the golden images, decorated around with *fundatum*. Indeed, above the fountains he made nine white silk curtains, decorated around with *fundatum*.

Here, at the place mentioned above, he clad the altar of the most blessed confessor and pontiff Leo in the purest gilded silver, weighing 109 pounds altogether. Likewise, he clad the altar of the confessor and pontiff Gregory in the purest gilded silver, weighing 127 pounds all around.

### 411

This prefect of God and distinguished pontiff clad and decorated the altar of the holy Apostle Paul in the purest silver; it weighed 155 pounds. He also clad his confession and the front of the altar in the purest gold, weighing 121 pounds and 8 ounces there. Above, at the entrance to the body of the church, he made a shield of the purest silver, on which he had the Creed of the orthodox faith inscribed; it weighed 32 pounds. At the place mentioned above he made three large crowns of the purest silver, weighing 93 pounds altogether. In the basilica he made a most beautiful large silk curtain of *quadrapulum* and *fundatum*.

The aforesaid venerable and distinguished pontiff made, in the basilica of the holy Apostle Peter, his nurturer, above the high altar, a ciborium with its four columns of the purest gilded silver, magnificently decorated with various scenes and of extraordinary size. It weighed 2,704 pounds and 3 ounces. The ciborium that he removed from there he placed above the high altar in the basilica of the blessed Mother of God, which is called at the Praesepe; and he made a cross of pure silver and placed it there, weighing 12 pounds and 3 ounces.

He also made four red *tetravela alithyna* at the place mentioned above, one of them with *chrysoclavus*. In the mausoleum of the blessed Petronilla, situated at the church of the holy Apostle Peter, he made three large white curtains and eight smaller ones, decorated around with *fundatum*.

The same distinguished pontiff made, before the confession of that prince of the Apostles, angels of the purest silver on the right and left, weighing 146 pounds there. He also made two other angels of the purest gilded silver, standing on the great beam above the entrance to the vestibule, on the right and left beside the golden image of the Savior; they weighed 63 pounds altogether. And four other smaller angels of the purest gilded silver, at the place mentioned above, on the right and left; they weighed 68 pounds altogether.

Furthermore, at the place mentioned above he made six small columns of gilded silver at the entrance of the vestibule, painted with various scenes; they weighed 147 pounds altogether. He also made a large cross of the purest gilded silver, standing beside the high altar; it weighed 22 pounds. At the place mentioned above he made a large arch of the purest gilded silver above the entrance of the vestibule; it weighed 131 and a half pounds. At the place mentioned above, inside the confession of the confessor and pontiff Leo, he made a Gospel-book of the purest gilded silver above the entrance of the vestibule; it weighed 48 and a half pounds. At the place mentioned above he made one small column of the purest silver, weighing 17 pounds.

This pontiff, protected by God and distinguished, made in the diaconia of the holy Archangel a paten and chalice of the purest silver, weighing 10 pounds together.

### 412

Here, protected by divine inspiration, he made in the basilica of the Savior, which is called Constantinian, a ciborium with its four columns of the purest silver, painted with various scenes and magnificently decorated with its screens and small columns, of extraordinary size and beauty; these weighed 1,227 pounds altogether.

Furthermore, he completely restored anew the roof and fabric of the basilica of the holy Mother of God, ever-Virgin Mary, our Lady, which is called at the Praesepe. The chambers beside the church of the blessed Peter, prince of the Apostles, had decayed through extreme old age and were almost collapsing. This outstanding prelate, laying the firmest foundations from the ground up, raised them again in a better condition. At the place mentioned above, beside the large column, he also built a bathhouse situated above, constructed in a circular form and magnificently decorated.

He restored anew the steps at the entrance of that basilica, both those above the portico and those in the atrium. Beside these steps, on the right side of the atrium, he built from the foundations a house of extraordinary size and beauty, in which he also placed couches.

[Col. 1239]

Beside that house he built, for the support of Christ’s poor and of pilgrims, a bathhouse from the foundations, magnificently decorated.

This distinguished bishop, inspired by God, newly built from the foundations a hospital for the holy Apostle Peter at the place called the Naumachia. There he decorated various buildings and constructed anew a church in honor of blessed Peter, prince of the Apostles. In it he also deposited the bodies of the holy martyrs of the Church of Christ, bringing them there, and constructed everything necessary in the aforesaid hospital.

### 413

There too he offered urban and rural estates for the sustenance of Christ’s poor, as well as of strangers and pilgrims who come from distant regions, for the exaltation of the holy Church of God and the safety of the Roman people.

In particular, the monastery of the holy first martyr of Christ, Stephen, which is called Catagalla Patritia, had already decayed from extreme old age and had partly collapsed. The same prophetic pontiff, undertaking the work, raised it again in a better condition from the foundations, together with the oratory, laying a firm foundation.

The steps by which he entered the church of the holy Apostle Peter from the church of the holy Apostle Andrew, which had been worn away by age, he rebuilt anew. Likewise, he almost entirely restored from the foundations the monastery of the blessed confessor and pontiff Martin, situated at the place mentioned above, which had been greatly weakened by age. He newly restored the roof and fabric of the basilica of the holy Apostle Andrew, which is called Catabarbara Patritia and whose structure had long since been consumed by age. In the same way he rebuilt anew the roof and fabric of the blessed martyr Lucia, situated at the Orpheus. He likewise restored for the better the roof and fabric of the blessed martyr Balbina, which were already almost collapsing. In the same way he magnificently restored the roof and fabric of the basilica of the blessed martyrs Cosmas and Damian, situated on the Sacred Way. He likewise restored for the better the roof and fabric of the basilica of the holy martyr Martina, situated at the Three Fates.

### 414

He also newly restored the roof and fabric of the title of the holy martyr Lawrence, which is called that of Damasus.

This most holy and distinguished pontiff magnificently rebuilt anew the roof and fabric of the basilica of the martyr Valentine, situated on the Via Flaminia, which were already about to collapse from excessive old age. He repaired anew, inside and outside, all the roof and fabric of the four-sided portico of the basilica of the Apostles on the Via Lata. Moreover, he newly repaired the roof and fabric of the basilica of the blessed martyr Agatha, situated above the Subura, which had already decayed through extreme old age.

This most holy prelate built from the foundations, in the Lateran patriarchate, an oratory in honor of the holy Archangel, constructing it with notable workmanship and the greatest solidity. He also decorated it throughout with mosaic, various paintings, and beautiful marble of different colors. There he offered all kinds of furnishings, both gold and silver, as well as various curtains.

The *macrona* of that Lateran patriarchate, which extends from the Campus and beyond the images of the Apostles, was already about to collapse from excessive old age. He restored its foundations, roof and fabric, and also its upper terrace, anew from bottom to top; he relaid it for the better with very firm marble; he newly made the ceiling of that *macrona* and magnificently decorated it with paintings of various scenes.

This venerable and distinguished pontiff, protected by God, made around the altar of the holy Apostle Peter, his nurturer, red silk *tetravela alithyna*, having panels or roundels of *chrysoclavus*, painted with various scenes, with stars of *chrysoclavus*. In the middle they also had crosses of *chrysoclavus* decorated with pearls, of extraordinary size and beauty; these are hung there on feast days as adornment.

Likewise, as above, he made other white, rose-colored silk *tetravela paschatilia*, having panels and roundels of *chrysoclavus*, as well as crosses with *chrysoclavus* made of pearls, with a *periclysin* of *chrysoclavus*. Moreover, he made four other small curtains at the place mentioned above, one on each column of the ciborium, having tigers of *chrysoclavus* and decorated around with *blatthinum*. Furthermore, he placed four other small curtains of the same appearance in the basilica of the teacher of the world, the blessed Apostle Paul, on the columns of the ciborium.

### 415

The aforesaid venerable pontiff restored anew and for the better all the roof and fabric of the basilica of the blessed martyr Agapitus, situated in the city of Praeneste, as well as the roof and fabric of another basilica situated beside that same basilica, which were already about to collapse from excessive old age.

Likewise, he newly repaired the roof and fabric of the basilica of the blessed first martyr Stephen, situated on the Via Latina at the third milestone, which had been worn out by many years of age and was near ruin. Furthermore, he newly restored the roof and fabric of the basilica of the blessed martyr Basilides, situated on the Merulana.

This venerable and distinguished pontiff, protected by God, made in the basilica of the Savior, our Lord Jesus Christ, which is called Constantinian, from the basilica’s own silver, five crowns with their dolphins, thirty-five canisters, and eight *gabathae*, weighing 276 pounds altogether.

In the basilica of the holy Mother of God, ever-Virgin Mary, our Lady, which is called at the Praesepe, he made a *fundata* curtain, decorated around with *blatthinum*, hanging in the portico above the seat and magnificently decorated. Forty miscellaneous curtains, some of *fundatum* and others of *stauracium* and *quadrapulum*, decorated around with *blatthinum*. At the place mentioned above, before the entrance to the

[Col. 1241]

Praesepe, he made a net-shaped *pharus* of the purest silver with five canisters, weighing 37 and a half pounds altogether.

### 416

This most holy prelate, filled with the illumination of the Holy Spirit, made for the holy Apostle Peter, his nurturer, a distinguished tetragonal golden chalice, *Spanoclystum*, adorned with various precious stones, weighing 32 pounds. He also made a golden paten, *Spanoclysta*, magnificently decorated, weighing 25 pounds and 9 ounces.

In the basilica mentioned above he made a net-shaped *pharus* with a canister and silver crosses of the purest silver, which hangs beneath the principal gold [ornament]. He also made another larger net-shaped *pharus*, with twenty canisters, hanging beneath the large silver beam, for the adornment of the holy Church of God; it weighed 2,104 pounds and 7 ounces there.

Here he made, in the basilica of the teacher of the world, the blessed Apostle Paul, a crucifix of the purest silver, magnificently fashioned and of extraordinary size, weighing 52 pounds. Furthermore, at the place mentioned above he made white, rose-colored silk *tetravela*, one of which had in the middle a cross of *chrysoclavus* and *gammadia* of *chrysoclavus*. He also made nine white silk curtains, decorated around with Tyrian [purple].

There he made eight *fundatae interrasiles* *gabathae* of the purest silver, hanging in the bronze *pharus* in the middle of the basilica; they weighed 14 pounds there.

The entrance to the body of the church the same prelate decorated with white marble in marvelous fashion, and there he installed bronze doors. Above the marble columns standing around the altar of that teacher of the world, where wooden beams had once been placed and had decayed through extreme old age, this holy bishop had lilies installed upon those columns; above the lilies he placed marble slabs (*platoniae*), and decorated the work with paintings of various kinds and extraordinary size.

At the place mentioned above he also made five large Alexandrian curtains, hanging above the large doors at the entrance of the basilica and magnificently decorated.

### 417

This most holy and distinguished pontiff made, in the basilica of the holy Mother of God, ever-Virgin Mary, our Lady, at the Praesepe, white, rose-colored silk *tetravela*, magnificently decorated.

At the place mentioned above, inside the Praesepe, he made a white, rose-colored silk vestment, decorated around with *chrysoclavus* and having in the middle a cross with roundels of *chrysoclavus*, and four white, rose-colored silk curtains, decorated around with Tyrian [purple].

In the diaconia of that same Mother of God, which is called Dominica, he made a white, rose-colored silk vestment, having in the middle a panel of Tyrian [purple] with the scene of the Crucifixion. Also, roundels of *chrysoclavus*, decorated around with *quadrapulum*. At the place mentioned above he made a *fundata* curtain, decorated around with *blatthinum*.

In the diaconia of that same Mother of God, which is called Cosmedin, he made a white silk vestment with a panel of *chrysoclavus*, bearing the scene of the Lord’s Resurrection, and around it a band of *chrysoclavus*.

At Saint Mary at the Martyrs he made a white, rose-colored silk vestment with a panel of Tyrian [purple], bearing the scene of the Crucifixion, and a roundel of *chrysoclavus*, decorated around with Tyrian [purple].

He also made, in the diaconia of the aforesaid holy Mother of God situated outside the gate of the holy Apostle Peter, a vestment of Tyrian [purple], magnificently decorated.

### 418

This venerable and distinguished pontiff made for the basilica of the blessed apostle Peter, his patron, openwork baskets of the purest silver, both in the quadriporticus and within the body of the basilica, twenty-two in number, weighing altogether 125 pounds. He also made forty-eight *fundatum signochrystae* basins, which hang in the quadriporticus, in the bronze pharos in the middle of the basilica; they weighed altogether 101½ pounds. Three silver pharoi, standing upon silver beams, weighed 93 pounds. Two silver arches weighed 41 pounds and 8 ounces.

Large *blatthin* curtains, which hang from the silver beams on the right and left of the presbytery. Likewise, around the throne, thirty in number, ornamented around the edge with *quadrapulum*. Forty-seven small *fundatum* curtains, ornamented around the edge with Byzantine *blatthin* and lined with Neapolitan *blatthin*.

Likewise, within the body of the basilica he made a larger Alexandrian curtain, of extraordinary size and beauty, ornamented around the edge with Tyrian [purple]. Twenty-five small white rose-colored silk curtains, ornamented around the edge with *blatthin*, one of them decorated with *stauracium*.

Above the altar of the blessed Andrew, in the place mentioned above, he made a white rose-colored silk vestment, with a panel of *chrysoclave*, displaying the story of the Lord’s Resurrection, and with a border of *chrysoclave* around it. Likewise, above the altar of the blessed Petronilla he made a white rose-colored silk vestment, with a panel of *chrysoclave*, displaying the story of the Lord’s Resurrection, and with a border of *chrysoclave* around it.

In the same way, in the oratory of the holy Mother of God, mentioned above, in the central section, he made a white rose-colored silk vestment, having in the middle a cross of *chrysoclave* and ornamented around it with Tyrian [purple]. In the oratory of that same Mother of God, mentioned above, which is called that of Pope Paul, he made a white silk vestment, ornamented around the edge with *mizilo*. Likewise, in the monastery of Saint Martin, mentioned above, he made a white rose-colored silk vestment, having in the middle a cross of *chrysoclave* with a *periclysis* of Tyrian [purple].

In the basilica of the Apostles on the Via Lata, he made above the high altar a white rose-colored silk vestment, having in the middle a panel of *stauracium* with the story of the Lord’s Resurrection, and around it a vestment of *chrysoclave*. Likewise, small disks of *chrysoclave*, with a *periclysis* of Tyrian [purple].

Four small red *tetravela*, ornamented around the edge with *fundatum*, one of them with *chrysoclave*.

[Col. 1243] Two small red Alexandrian curtains, ornamented around the edge with *stauracium*. Within the body of the basilica, mentioned above, he made a larger *fundatum* curtain, magnificently decorated and ornamented around the edge with Tyrian [purple], and having crosses of Tyrian [purple] in the middle.

### 419

This distinguished prelate made in the title-church of the holy martyr Sabina, above the high altar, a white rose-colored silk vestment, having in the middle a panel of *stauracium* with the story of the Lord’s Resurrection, and around it a border of *chrysoclave*. In the same way, in the title-church of the holy martyr Susanna, above the high altar, he made a white rose-colored silk vestment, having in the middle a panel of *chrysoclave* with the story of the Lord’s Resurrection, and around it a border of *chrysoclave*.

In the basilica of Saint Stephen the protomartyr on the Caelian Hill he made a white rose-colored silk vestment, having in the middle a panel of *stauracium* with the story of the Lord’s Resurrection, and a cross of *chrysoclave*. Likewise, in the diaconia of the blessed martyr George, above the high altar, he made a white rose-colored silk vestment, having in the middle a panel of *stauracium* with the story of the Crucified One, ornamented with Tyrian [purple], and roses of *chrysoclave*.

This venerable and distinguished pontiff, protected by God, made in the basilica of the holy Mother of God called “at the Crèche,” out of his great love for our Lady herself, a pharos of the purest silver, with its lamp and lamp-holder,

[Note: [Col. 1243] B reads *cerapto* for *cereapto*.]

weighing altogether 40½ pounds. His Beatitude appointed that on Sundays and on holy solemnities it should stand beside the lectern, so that, for the reading of the sacred lessons, it might shine with the splendor of its light.

In the church of the blessed apostle Peter he likewise made a pharos of the purest gilded silver, decorated with extraordinary beauty, with its lamp and lamp-holder, which together weighed 90½ pounds. Indeed, in the place mentioned above, at the shrine of the blessed apostle Peter, beneath the image of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ crucified, he made a crown of the purest silver and placed it there, for the splendor of the lights, out of love for our Lord Jesus Christ; it weighed … pounds.

### 420

The basilica of the blessed martyr and bishop Apollinaris, which was founded beside the city of Ravenna, had beams that, because of their excessive age over the passage of many years and from ancient times, had decayed greatly and at that time were almost on the point of collapse. This same venerable Father, divinely inspired, sent men there and, through his most diligent and prudent care, entirely restored anew and firmly all the roofing of that church together with its quadriporticus, bringing it back to a better condition.

Above the altar of that sacred basilica, in honor of almighty God and the blessed apostle Peter, from whose gifts and donations he made a rose-colored silk vestment, having in the middle a cross of *chrysoclave* with disks, and silk wheels displaying the scenes of the Annunciation; the birth of our Lord Jesus Christ; the Passion and Resurrection; and also the Ascension into heaven and Pentecost. They were ornamented around the edge in the same manner as the vestment of *chrysoclave*.

He also made there a basket of the purest silver with its little chains, weighing 15 pounds.

The Alban episcopal residence, together with the church founded in the name of the blessed Pancratius, was, through some negligence or carelessness and through diabolical promptings, burned after the morning praises; it was consumed by fire from its foundations to the highest part of the roof. But the most merciful and diligent pontiff, with God inspiring him through the illumination of the Holy Spirit, laying a firm foundation, rebuilt anew in a marvelous manner the church mentioned above and, with its roofing restored, brought it, with God’s help, into a better condition.

### 421

And as a true lover of God and worshiper of the holy churches of God, he made above the high altar of the aforesaid church two vestments. Of these, one had larger wheels bearing griffins and was ornamented around the edge with *fundatum*; and he made four silk *tetravela* of genuine *alithyna*, ornamented around the edge of the same altar with excellent Tyrian [purple].

Likewise, in the church of the blessed apostle Peter, mentioned above, he made a rose-colored vestment displaying the scene of our Lord Jesus Christ when he extended his hands and seized the blessed apostle Peter from the waves of the sea.

This same most blessed and distinguished pontiff made in the basilica of Saint Cyriacus a white silk vestment having, around its circumference, a *periclysis* of *fundatum* and, in the middle, the story of the Resurrection; and around the altar, white *tetravela* having a *periclysis* of Tyrian [purple].

He also made in the title-church of Saint Vitalis a white silk vestment having a *periclysis* of *fundatum* and, in the middle, the story of the Resurrection. Likewise, in the diaconia of the holy Archangel he placed a white silk vestment having a *periclysis* of Tyrian [purple] and, in the middle, the story of the Ascension. He also offered a similar vestment above the altar of Saint Abbacyrus.

Moreover, in the diaconia of the holy martyr Agatha this most holy pontiff made a white silk vestment having around it Tyrian [purple] and, in the middle, the story of the Resurrection.

Likewise, in the title-church of Pammachius, above the altar of Saints John and Paul, he made a white silk vestment ornamented around with *fundatum*, displaying the stories of the Crucifixion, Ascension, and Pentecost.

In the church of the blessed martyr and bishop Clement he likewise made a white vestment with *chrysoclave*, displaying the story of the Resurrection, or of the Ascension, and also Pentecost.

[Col. 1245]

### 422

Moreover, in the church of Saint Cyriacus situated on the Ostian Way, he made five *quadrapulum* curtains, displaying the story of the Savior calling his disciples from the boat. Above the holy altar of that martyr he placed a *fundatum* vestment.

This distinguished pontiff, protected by God, made in the basilica of the holy Mother of God, ever-Virgin Mary, our lady, at the Crèche, silver crowns and their twelve dolphins, weighing 102 pounds and 9 ounces. He also made there seven silver *phara-canthera* with their dolphins, weighing 85½ pounds.

The same blessed prelate made in the basilica of the blessed apostle Peter, his patron, before the presbytery, a movable pharos of the purest silver, with crowns and crosses, weighing there 35 pounds and 6 ounces.

Likewise, below, where the most sacred body of that prince of the apostles rests, he renewed a golden image bearing the faces of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, the holy Mother of God Mary, our lady, and the blessed apostles Peter, Paul, and Andrew, as well as the blessed martyr Petronilla. There he also added 21 pounds and 3 ounces of refined gold.

### 423

Indeed, in the place mentioned above, before Saint Andrew, he covered the altar of the blessed confessor Martin with gilded silver, from a former bequest of Abbot Fridigius,

[Note: [Col. 1245] B reads “from the property formerly belonging to Abbot Fridigius.”]

which weighed altogether 17½ pounds.

He also made in the basilica of the blessed apostle Paul, teacher of the nations, a *phara-canthera* of the purest silver with five dolphins, weighing 67 pounds and 4 ounces.

### 424

This venerable and distinguished pontiff, inspired by God, seeing that the church of the blessed martyrs Nereus and Achilleus was failing because of excessive age and was being filled by the overflowing of waters, built beside that same church, anew from its foundations and on higher ground, a church of extraordinary size and beauty. In it he also offered these gifts:

Six silver baskets, weighing altogether 15 pounds; a ciborium of the purest silver, weighing 215 pounds; a chalice and paten of the purest gilded silver, weighing 12 pounds and 10 ounces; a crown above the altar of the purest gold, adorned with various precious stones, weighing 2 pounds and 6 ounces; and two vestments, one of them white silk, displaying the stories of the Lord’s Nativity or Resurrection, Ascension, and Pentecost, ornamented around the edge with *chrysoclave*, and the other of Tyrian [purple].

The same man made in the basilica of the blessed Mother of God at the Crèche a crown of the purest *Spanoclystus* gold, ornamented around the edge with various precious stones and *chrysoclave*, weighing 4 pounds and 7 ounces.

He made silver *communicalia* for the individual districts, to precede the processions at the stations, carried by acolytes, twenty-four in number, weighing altogether …

Likewise, in the basilica of the blessed apostle Peter, his supporter, he made a crown of the purest gold, adorned with various precious stones, weighing 7 pounds.

He also made in the diaconia of Saints Nereus and Achilleus miscellaneous silk curtains, number …

### 425

He restored anew the roofing of the blessed martyr Agapitus, situated beside the basilica of the blessed martyr Lawrence outside the wall, because it had already decayed through excessive age.

Indeed, in the title-church of the blessed Pudentiana he made a white silk vestment ornamented around the edge with Tyrian [purple].

This most blessed pontiff, after having ruled the Roman and apostolic see most gloriously for twenty years, five months, and sixteen days, was taken from this light and departed to eternal rest. He held three ordinations in the month of March: thirty priests, eleven deacons, and 126 bishops in various places

[Note: [Col. 1245] B reads 26.]

He was buried in the basilica of the apostle Peter on the day before the Ides of June, in the ninth indiction, and the episcopate was vacant for ten days.

## XCIX. STEPHANUS V. IN THE YEAR OF CHRIST 816; OF THE EMPEROR LOUIS, 3; OF THE EMPEROR LEO THE ARMENIAN, 3

[Note: [Col. 1257A]

In Fabrottus, from the Freher manuscript:

No. 426, line 1: “he held office seven months.” Line 6: “he practiced worthy habits of humility.”

No. 427, line 1: “he advanced him to the order of deacon.” Line 9: “pope of the city.”

No. 428, line 2: “he undertook the journey to Francia.”

From the Royal, Mazarine, and Thuane manuscripts:
